recent_posts.title: Beyond the Pilot: Building the Clinical Data Fabric for the Agentic Era
recent_posts.summary: A Cisco CX executive reflects on a panel about scaling AI in healthcare, arguing that the industry is entering an 'Agentic Era' where AI systems act autonomously rather than just summarizing data. The core thesis is that the bottleneck is no longer algorithmic but infrastructural: healthcare data is too large to move efficiently, so compute must be brought to the data at the point of care. This requires rethinking the network as a 'clinical data fabric' with low-latency architecture, end-to-end observability, predictive operations, and zero-trust security. The piece frames agentic AI as a solution to clinician burnout by offloading administrative cognitive load.

recent_posts.title: Try Cisco AI Defense Explorer Edition in this hands-on lab
recent_posts.summary: Cisco AI Defense Explorer Edition is an agentic red-teaming tool that adapts attacks across multiple conversation turns to test AI models and applications before deployment. A hands-on DevNet lab (~40 minutes) walks through connecting a customer support assistant target, running a Quick Scan with a custom objective focused on hidden instruction disclosure, and reviewing findings including Attack Success Rate across 14 risk categories, custom goals, and system prompt extraction results.

recent_posts.title: From Bandwidth to Intelligence: How Cisco is Powering AI-Ready Networks
recent_posts.summary: Cisco's perspective on how AI is fundamentally reshaping network infrastructure for service providers and telcos. AI traffic patterns — bursty, latency-sensitive, and unpredictable — are straining conventional network designs, requiring a shift toward intelligent, adaptive systems. Cisco promotes a full-stack approach including predictive demand-aware design using Crosswork and ThousandEyes, autonomous operations with AI-driven anomaly detection, and software-driven scale via Segment Routing. The post also outlines monetization opportunities: outage reduction, smarter capacity planning via digital twins, premium AI-ready connectivity tiers, edge AI services, and network slicing for application-aware performance. A podcast with Lumen's Distinguished Engineer is referenced as a real-world example of adapting networks for AI workloads.

recent_posts.title: Spotlight on digital transformation | FY25 Purpose Report
recent_posts.summary: Cisco's FY25 Purpose Report highlights its Country Digital Acceleration (CDA) program's 10-year anniversary, showcasing digital transformation projects across Canada, Italy, India, and Saudi Arabia. The report also covers Cisco's learning initiatives under the 'Learn with Cisco' umbrella, including Networking Academy, Cisco U., and new AI-focused courses. Notable milestones include empowering over one million Brazilian learners, expanding to 195 countries in eight languages, and launching AI/ML training resources to address a gap where 87% of instructors recognize AI's importance but only 10% feel equipped to teach it.

recent_posts.title: Galaxy Mode is live: A limited-time look at what your Cisco AI Assistant and AgenticOps can already do
recent_posts.summary: Cisco has launched 'Galaxy Mode', a Star Wars-themed limited-time experience (May 4 – June 4) inside the Cisco AI Assistant for Meraki and ThousandEyes. Beyond the cosmetic theme, the announcement highlights AgenticOps capabilities: end-to-end agentic troubleshooting, AI-powered workflow creation via natural language in the Meraki dashboard, and beta features including image upload analysis and Deep Reasoning mode for multi-domain signal interpretation. The post frames this as a shift from reactive network operations to AI-orchestrated, autonomous NetOps.

recent_posts.title: Securing the Agentic Workforce: Cisco Announces Intent to Acquire Astrix Security
recent_posts.summary: Cisco has announced its intent to acquire Astrix Security, a specialist in Non-Human Identity (NHI) security. The acquisition aims to extend Cisco's Zero Trust architecture to cover AI agents and non-human identities such as API keys, OAuth tokens, and service accounts. Astrix Security's capabilities include discovery and governance for AI agents, agentic access lifecycle management, threat detection and response, and secrets management. Cisco plans to integrate these capabilities into Cisco Identity Intelligence, Cisco Secure Access, and Duo IAM, giving security teams unified visibility across identity, network, application, and infrastructure layers to govern and respond to agent activity at machine speed.

recent_posts.title: Understanding CISA BOD 26-02: Mitigating Risk from End-of-Support Edge Devices
recent_posts.summary: CISA issued Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-02 on February 5, 2026, requiring Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to address security risks from End-of-Support (EOS) edge devices like firewalls, routers, and VPN gateways. The directive sets a two-year compliance timeline: agencies must inventory EOS devices by May 2026, begin replacements by February 2027, complete removals by August 2027, and establish continuous lifecycle management by February 2028. Cisco promotes its FedRAMP-authorized Security Cloud for Government portfolio—including Security Cloud Control, Secure Access for Government, Meraki, Duo Federal, and SD-WAN—as cloud-native solutions that reduce hardware dependency and help agencies meet BOD 26-02 compliance deadlines.

recent_posts.title: The impact of AI on wide area network traffic: we need to talk
recent_posts.summary: Cisco has published a research report examining how AI—particularly agentic AI—is reshaping wide area network (WAN) traffic patterns. Based on live production network data and controlled experiments, the report finds that AI inference traffic behaves fundamentally differently from standard web traffic in terms of shape, symmetry, latency requirements, and criticality. Key projections include AI inference representing 25% of all network traffic by 2035, with the sharpest growth between 2029 and 2032, and a 63% additional traffic growth driven by AI's multiplying effect. The report argues that traditional network planning assumptions are no longer valid and calls for updated infrastructure strategies, including differentiated QoS, higher resilience, and continuous measurement frameworks for network leaders and service providers.

recent_posts.title: Digging Deeper: The Future of Mining with Automation and Ultra-Reliable Wireless
recent_posts.summary: Modern mining operations are increasingly relying on automation technologies like autonomous haulage systems, AI-driven predictive maintenance, and tele-remote operations. The effectiveness of these systems depends entirely on ultra-reliable wireless connectivity. Cisco's Catalyst IW9167E Heavy Duty Access Point combined with Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul (URWB) provides zero-packet-loss, low-latency connectivity designed for harsh mining environments. Cisco offers validated design guides and industry partnerships (including Caterpillar) to ensure proven deployments, with real-world use cases like supporting tele-remote dam decommissioning with Aterpa.

recent_posts.title: Built like a startup, scaled like Cisco: Transforming data center cooling for the AI era
recent_posts.summary: Cisco engineers describe building a direct-liquid-cooled network switch from prototype to product, driven by the surging power demands of AI GPU racks. AI racks now draw 60–130 kW and are projected to reach 1 MW by 2030, making air cooling inadequate. A small internal team debuted a prototype at OFC 2023, solved the hard problem of cooling hot-swappable 800G OSFP optics with a novel 2×8 cold-plate design, and used strong customer feedback to secure leadership buy-in. The resulting Cisco N9000/8000 systems with Silicon One G300 deliver 102.4 Tbps throughput with a ~70% energy improvement over prior generations. Cisco also launched an Engineering Alliances program to accelerate ecosystem integration and is exploring immersion cooling and liquid-cooling for storage and power supplies.
